operative_clauses.judgment_reason: The order excuses the listed society members from duty so that they may take part in the parade in connection with the removal of the body of the Vice-President; its text states "Vice-President Clinton on Wednesday, May 27, 1908, be excused from". The excusal therefore ran to May 27, 1908, recorded inclusive (it covers that whole day); the exclusive reading is that it ends when that day begins.

research_rationale:
EO 799 (signed 1908-05-23 by Theodore Roosevelt, held ProQuest scan text) excuses from duty, for the parade in connection with the removal of the body of Vice-President Clinton on May 27, 1908, the listed patriotic-society members employed in the District of Columbia in the executive departments and independent establishments. The Register and WPA entry for 1908 May 23 p.92 agree with the text on date and subject. The order is a single one-time permission with one clause and no later-reaching command. It is spent by its own terms on the stated day: May 27, 1908 is recorded inclusive (the excusal covers that whole day), the exclusive reading being that it ends when that day begins. Held searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no hit for this order, and the corpus search for the number found only the Wikisource neighbour-navigation pages of EO 798 and EO 800, which are not later events affecting it.

Superseded Executive Order 1087, June 15, 1909.

Signed by President William H. Taft Monday, June 21, 1909

592332Executive Order 1093 — Authorizing Reinstatement of Hattie M. Miller as Skilled Laborer in Patent Office1909President of the United States

Miss Hattie M. Miller, having been formerly a skilled laborer in the Patent Office of the Interior Department with an excellent record, and having been voluntarily separated from the service for more than a year, may be reinstated as a skilled laborer in the Patent Office of the Interior Department without reference to the length of time she has been separated from the service. This order is made upon the recommendation of the Commissioner of Patents that it is in the interest of the efficiency of the service thus to restore Miss Miller.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

June 21, 1909.

research_rationale:
EO 1087 (signed 1909-06-15 by William H. Taft; held Wikisource revision 1766830) permits Miss Hattie M. Miller to be reinstated in the Patent Office as a classified laborer at $600 without regard to the length of time since her separation. The Register and WPA entry (1909 June 15 p.115, 1909 CSR 131) agree on person, grade and date. The held Wikisource text of EO 1093 (signed 1909-06-21) authorizes reinstating the same person in the same office as a skilled laborer and carries the editorial annotation "Superseded Executive Order 1087, June 15, 1909."; the held page of EO 1087 carries the matching annotation. The end is recorded as supersession by EO 1093 on 1909-06-21. Disclosure: the supersession word appears in the transcription's annotation, not in EO 1093's own operative sentence, which grants a replacement reinstatement of the same person; no held source shows whether a reinstatement under EO 1087 was actually made before 1093. The name-match lead EO 4131 (ProQuest scan) is an unrelated order on Alaska military reservations and does not mention this order or this person. Machine searches (U.S. Code, eCFR, OFR catalog) found no hits for EO 1087.

Miller as a classified laborer. EO 1093 replaces it for the same person and office."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 1087 is a one-person permission to reinstate; its operative effect was replaced by EO 1093 for the same person and office. No held source shows any surviving command, and any personnel action taken under it would be a completed act, not a continuing order.
